newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close weak as soybeans collapse.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close weak as soybeans collapse.

text.p: CBOT soy products closed weaker on Tuesday as soybeans collapsed late amid bearish fundemental and technical indicators, traders said.
"The bean market struggled all day yesterday and corn bailed it out. Corn didn't bail it out today," a trader said.

Traders noted Korea turned to Indian supplies to fill a 43,800-tonne soymeal tender. While the move was not surprising, it confirmed speculation that U.S. supplies would take a back seat to Indian products.
Dealers said buyers were uncomfortable purchasing large amounts of meal in a volatile market.
While U.S. supplies are normally shipped in 50,000-tonne capacity Panamaxes, Indian soymeal can be sent in smaller 10,000-tonne vessels, traders said.
Forecasts for rain later this week in dry Brazilian soybean growing regions also pressured the market and alleviated concerns of drought-related crop losses.
"It's isolated (dry) spots," said Eloi Hilgert of the Rio Grande do Sul agricultural secretariat. "There's no indication of any crop loss yet."
Soyoil ended down 0.20 to 0.12 cent a lb. Soymeal finished down $1.70 to $0.50 per ton with March off $1.20 at $236.90.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 300 lots March soymeal and sold 200 lots. Dean Witter bought 300 lots March.
In soyoil, ADM sold 200 lots May, Cargill Inc sold 200 March and bought 100 March and Central Soya sold 100 March.
Volume in soymeal was estimated by the CBOT at 12,000 lots, against Monday's actual volume of 13,504 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 8,500 lots against Monday's 7,416 lots.
